description: Wanderer. He maps the Drift with stakes and string, walks the eastern line every year, and has stopped telling anybody what the measurements say.
lore: Most people meet a Turn the morning after, when the path goes somewhere new. Gunnar meets it in the numbers. He walks the country with stakes and knotted string and a ledger of small tidy figures, re-measuring what everyone else re-remembers, and for years he did it out loud — sheets posted at the fires, a hamlet warned its ford was going, the shore people told which cliff not to build under. They thanked him and built there anyway, or moved and grumbled, and either way the maps did what maps are for.

Then his eastern line began coming back wrong in one direction only. Soft ground — the kind that forgets faster than anyone is forgetting it — moving year on year, not wandering the way the Drift wanders but travelling, and travelling toward the meadow. [[lore/the_hole_under_the_mountain|The Hole Under the Mountain]] says he has stopped telling anybody what he measures, and it is so. The spring he was sure, he walked to the meadow fire, sat down across from [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]], accepted the second cup, and talked for an hour about the weather. Then he thanked her and left. He has made that walk three springs running.

His reasoning is as tidy as the ledger: a fright helps no one who cannot act on it; the fires cannot move a meadow; so the knowing should sit with the one man fit to carry it. That is also why he has never gone on — you cannot leave, he says, in the middle of a measurement. The flaw in the reasoning is not on his maps. It is in the man: he has mistaken carrying a thing alone for keeping people safe from it, and the ground is not slowing down.
gm_notes: Agrees with the_hole_under_the_mountain (stopped telling anybody; the yearly eastern line) and adds the direction: the soft ground travels toward the meadow. A slow campaign clock the GM controls; his silence is the pacing valve — the day he says the numbers out loud is a session, not a sentence. The annual non-conversation with Solveig (the second cup, the weather) is a repeatable scene. Flaw: thinks knowing alone is protecting people. Supports B7 dread without advancing any beat.
